name: The Glessner household at 1706 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_glessner_george_m

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 1706 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903) and again in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904), which bracket 1 July 1904. The 1905 list prints: 1706 Mr. & Mrs. J. G. M. Glessner; Mrs. E. F. Hamlin.

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 1706, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. The 1900 census was read for the Prairie Avenue sheets of ED 36 and ED 40 (T623 roll 245), and this household was not found at this number on 1 June 1900, so no staff are listed. The 1910 census was not read. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

born.note: John and Frances Glessner's son, George Macbeth Glessner, born 1871 (the museum's family page); the Blue Book prints him 'J. G. M. Glessner'.

persons.note: The Blue Book's 'J. G. M. Glessner' at 1706 is the son of the house at 1800, which it lists separately; the Prairie library's reading of the page makes the same point. He moved his family to New Hampshire for good in 1915.
